15 unique neutral business question notes; no points before result
detail: This locates the part of work where momentum changes: beginning, switching, waiting or finishing. It gives a possible starting point for following a real task.
This asks how the next piece of work gets chosen. Choosing a priority and assigning its owner are separate parts of the picture.
This locates the knowledge a task depends on. Where information lives is different from whether the right person can use it at the moment it’s needed.
This describes the current mix of AI use, connection and consistency. It adds context about the tools in play; it isn’t a count of people or completed tasks.
This follows learning across the end of a project. It asks what carries into the next project, rather than how the current task gets completed.
This follows an inquiry after the first contact. It adds context about the path from someone showing interest to someone responding.
This asks how responsibility lands with a person. It keeps ownership distinct from priority, availability and the tool holding the task.
This describes how AI is used within the work. It adds the operating context around the tools: experimentation, workflows, rules and oversight.
This asks how a decision gets made when time or circumstances are pressing. It adds the decision path, rather than judging the outcome of any one decision.
This asks what keeps revenue-related follow-through moving. It adds context about the work people personally carry between steps.
This asks about work being done again. The answer identifies repetition to examine; it doesn’t establish whether that repetition was necessary.
This describes what changes when someone is away. It adds a continuity view that an ordinary day might not reveal.
This asks what can be seen about current opportunities. Visibility and follow-through are different, so I keep this alongside the questions about response and ownership.
This follows learning from execution back into the way work runs. It adds a view of ongoing adjustment, separate from what happens when a project ends.
This captures the overall feel of the business in the owner’s own assessment. I keep that view beside the more specific answers; the label isn’t a diagnosis.

8 unique personal question notes
detail: This is about the moment I try to begin. It separates starting conditions from what happens during the rest of my day.
This asks about finding something I’ve already saved. It adds context about retrieval, which can help me choose a starting spot for DDD.
This captures how the day feels when I put it down. It adds my experience of the day, rather than counting what I finished.
This asks about unfinished things I’m keeping track of. The number of open loops and where I keep them are different parts of that picture.
This follows an AI output into what happens next. It asks about my experience of using it, rather than how much the tool produced.
This imagines returning after some time away. It adds a view of where the context lives when it’s no longer fresh in my head.
This looks at where the morning goes. It adds a specific moment in the day, separate from the overall feeling I reported earlier.
This asks what relief would feel like to me. It keeps the reason for making a change connected to my own day.
